ei.title: Our Virtues: Not Impulsive and Instant, But Stable and Habitual
ei.subject: 10월_2024 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: Our Virtues: Not Impulsive and Instant, But Stable and Habitual

fullPassage: Imagine that your usually stingy friend delights in buying you a Christmas present after taking a generosity booster. How would you feel? Undoubtedly, there is something praiseworthy about the action. You'd be pleased to receive the gift. You'd say 'thank you', and mean it. But his change of heart is not entirely satisfying. According to Zagzebski, an American philosopher, he is not really generous. When we praise someone's character, we use words for various virtues: 'generous', 'kind', 'courageous', etc. A person who gives one gift isn't generous. Instead, generosity is a stable part of a person's 'moral identity', an emotional habit that is part of who you are. Thus virtues, as opposed to nontypical impulse, are the result of your personal history. They are part of who you are, as they are part of how your character was formed. Instant virtue is therefore impossible. Popping a pill cannot make you a better person.

questions.passage: Imagine that your usually (A)[stingy / generous] friend delights in buying you a Christmas present after taking a generosity booster. How would you feel? Undoubtedly, there is something (B)[praiseworthy / shameful] about the action. You'd be pleased to receive the gift. You'd say 'thank you', and mean it. But his change of heart is not entirely (C)[satisfying / frustrating]. According to Zagzebski, an American philosopher, he is not really generous. When we praise someone's character, we use words for various virtues: 'generous', 'kind', 'courageous', etc. A person who gives one gift isn't generous. Instead, generosity is a stable part of a person's 'moral identity', an emotional habit that is part of who you are. Thus virtues, as opposed to nontypical impulse, are the result of your personal history. They are part of who you are, as they are part of how your character was formed. Instant virtue is therefore impossible. Popping a pill cannot make you a better person.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① generous — praiseworthy — satisfying: (A) generous(관대한)는 stingy(인색한)의 반의어
❌ ② stingy — shameful — satisfying: (B) shameful(부끄러운)은 praiseworthy(칭찬할 만한)의 반의어
✅ ③ stingy — praiseworthy — satisfying: 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ stingy — praiseworthy — frustrating: (C) frustrating(좌절감을 주는)은 satisfying(만족스러운)의 반의어
det.tip: usually stingy friend / something praiseworthy / not entirely satisfying

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

❌ ③ pleased — 원문 일치. '선물을 받아서 기뻐할(pleased) 것이다'에 적절
❌ ④ generous — 원문 일치. '그는 진정으로 관대한(generous) 것이 아니다'에 적절
det.tip: something praiseworthy about the action — 그 행동에 칭찬할 만한 점이 있다

✅ ④ 의미하다 — 진심이다: (A) '결과가 의미하는 바는~' (B) '진심으로 말하다' ←정답
det.tip: (A) The results mean that~ = 결과가 ~을 의미하다 / (B) mean it = 진심이다

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"a good moral quality in a person, or the general quality of being morally good"

det.analysis:
❌ ① habit(습관): '도덕적으로 좋은 성질'과 다름
✅ ② virtue(미덕): '사람의 좋은 도덕적 성질' 정의에 정확히 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ impulse(충동): 도덕적 성질이 아닌 순간적 욕구
❌ ④ identity(정체성): 도덕적 성질이 아닌 자아 인식
det.tip: words for various virtues: 'generous', 'kind', 'courageous'

questions.passage: But his change of heart is not entirely __________. (satisfy) According to Zagzebski, an American philosopher, he is not really generous.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: be동사(is)의 보어 자리에 형용사가 필요하다. 주어 'his change of heart(그의 마음의 변화)'가 '만족감을 주는' 대상이므로, 현재분사형 감정형용사 satisfying(만족스러운)이 적절하다. cf) satisfied는 '만족하는(감정을 느끼는 주체)'
det.tip: 주어가 감정을 유발하는 대상 → 현재분사(-ing)

questions.passage: Thus virtues, as __________ (oppose) to nontypical impulse, are the result of your personal history.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 'as opposed to ~'는 '~와 대조적으로, ~와 달리'라는 관용구이다. 접속사 as 뒤에서 주절 주어 virtues와 수동 관계를 이루는 과거분사 opposed가 쓰인다. 'as (they are) opposed to ~'에서 주어+be동사가 생략된 구조.
det.tip: as opposed to ~ = ~와 대조적으로 (관용 표현)

questions.passage: Imagine that your usually stingy friend delights in buying you a Christmas present after taking a generosity booster. How would you feel? Undoubtedly, there is something praiseworthy about the action. You'd be pleased to receive the gift. You'd say 'thank you', and mean it. But his change of heart is not entirely satisfying. According to Zagzebski, an American philosopher, he is not really generous. When we praise someone's character, we use words for various virtues: 'generous', 'kind', 'courageous', etc. A person who gives one gift isn't generous. Instead, generosity is a stable part of a person's '__________', an emotional habit that is part of who you are. Thus virtues, as opposed to nontypical impulse, are the result of your personal history. They are part of who you are, as they are part of how your character was formed. Instant virtue is therefore impossible. Popping a pill cannot make you a better person.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: '관대함은 도덕적 정체성의 안정된 일부이다'의 빈칸. moral identity=도덕적 정체성
det.analysis:

❌ ② physical appearance(외모): 관대함은 내면적 특성으로 외모와 무관
✅ ③ moral identity(도덕적 정체성): 관대함이 도덕적 정체성의 안정된 일부라는 원문 맥락 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ personal interest(개인적 관심사): 관대함은 관심사가 아닌 미덕

det.korean: '미덕은 개인 역사의 결과이다'의 빈칸. personal history=개인 역사
det.analysis:
❌ ① natural talent(타고난 재능): 미덕은 타고난 것이 아니라 형성된 것이라는 글의 논지와 모순
